reviews.title: Unleash Peak Gaming Performance with Intel Core i7-13700KF!
reviews.comment:
The Intel Core i7-13700KF Gaming Desktop Processor is a powerhouse that delivers exceptional performance for gaming enthusiasts and content creators alike. With 16 cores (8 P-cores + 8 E-cores) and the ability to be unlocked, this processor is a game-changer in the world of desktop computing.
The combination of P-cores and E-cores provides a perfect balance between high-speed single-threaded performance and efficient multi-threaded capabilities. Whether you're conquering the latest AAA titles or engaging in content creation tasks, the i7-13700KF handles it with ease.
The unlocked nature of this processor caters to overclocking enthusiasts, allowing for fine-tuning to extract every ounce of performance. This feature is complemented by Intel's advanced cooling technologies, ensuring stable temperatures even under heavy workloads.
Gaming experiences are taken to new heights with the i7-13700KF, thanks to its high clock speeds and robust architecture. The processor effortlessly handles demanding games and applications, providing a smooth and immersive user experience.
Multitasking becomes a breeze with the ample core count, enabling seamless execution of multiple applications simultaneously. Whether you're streaming, video editing, or running virtual machines, the i7-13700KF excels in handling resource-intensive tasks.
The Intel Core i7-13700KF also supports the latest DDR5 memory technology, enhancing overall system responsiveness and data transfer speeds.
In conclusion, the Intel Core i7-13700KF Gaming Desktop Processor is a stellar choice for users who demand uncompromising performance. Whether you're a gamer seeking high frame rates or a content creator requiring processing power, this unlocked processor is a worthy investment that brings your desktop experience to a whole new level.

reviews.title: A Powerhouse for Gamers and Creators
reviews.comment: The Intel Core i7-13700K 16-core processor is a powerhouse CPU that strikes an impressive balance between gaming prowess and demanding productivity workloads. With its hybrid architecture, featuring a mix of performance and efficiency cores, it delivers exceptional multi-threaded performance that rivals other higher-end chips, making it a fantastic value for its price point. While it can run hot and is quite power-hungry under heavy loads, necessitating a robust cooling solution, its ability to handle intensive tasks like video editing, 3D rendering, and high-refresh-rate gaming with ease makes it a compelling choice for enthusiasts and professionals alike for consistent results.
reviews.author: C M

reviews.title: Fast! Worth the price
reviews.comment:
The Intel Core i7-13700KF presents a compelling value proposition for its price. As part of Intel's 13th Gen "Raptor Lake" series, it boasts a robust 8 Performance-core (P-core) and 8 Efficient-core (E-core) configuration, mirroring the previous-gen flagship i9-12900K but at a more accessible price point​​. This configuration, coupled with updates like larger L2 caches for P-cores and improved cache hardware-prefetchers, contributes to its outstanding performance.
In terms of raw performance, the i7-13700KF demonstrates commendable prowess. It outperforms the 12th gen flagship Core i9-12900K in single and multi-core tests, albeit marginally, and shows significant performance gains over its direct predecessor, the Core i7-12700K, with a 12% and 32.5% lead in single-core and multi-core tests, respectively​​. When compared to competitors like the AMD Ryzen 7 5800X and Ryzen 9 5950X, the i7-13700KF shows a remarkable 23% and 25% single-core performance bump, and an even more impressive 67% and 15% lead in multi-core performance against these AMD chips​​.
However, buyers should be aware that the Core i7-13700KF does not come with integrated graphics. For users who require onboard video capabilities, the slightly higher-priced Core i7-13700K would be the best choice. The absence of integrated graphics in the 13700KF model can be a significant consideration for those who don't plan to use a dedicated graphics card.
The i7-13700KF stands out as an excellent choice for its price, offering high-end performance that rivals even some flagship models from the previous generation. Its value is particularly notable when considering its performance metrics against direct competitors and predecessors

reviews.title: Solid Upgrade for Gaming and Multitasking
reviews.comment:
As a software engineer and avid gamer, I recently upgraded to this for my new build, and I'm pretty impressed so far. Cyberpunk 2077 runs much smoother now, even with all the settings cranked up. Multitasking is a breeze; I can stream, game, and have multiple apps open without any noticeable lag.
I haven't gotten deep into overclocking yet, but the initial results are promising. Thermals seem manageable with my current cooler, but I might invest in something beefier if I push it harder. It dropped right into my 700 series motherboard without any issues. For the price, it feels like a solid deal, especially considering the performance boost over my old CPU. I'm hoping this will keep my system relevant for a few years, and while it does draw more power, the performance gains are worth it for me.
reviews.author: ziyang c.

reviews.title: Awesome CPU, but you might need an AIO
reviews.comment:
Upgraded from an i3 12100F primarily to edit video and I'm very happy with the performance. Davinci Resolve was simply too much for the i3. With the i7, my render times dropped from an hour to 10 minutes and editing on the timeline is leaps and bounds smoother.
Now the bad...
When I swapped out the CPU, I kept my Cooler Master Hyper 212 120mm air cooler paired with the i7. For gaming, it was no problem. Temps averaged around 60c, which I could live with. When it came to rendering video however, temps would skyrocket to 100c and throttle. I ended up purchasing a Cooler Master Master Liquid 360L Core AIO and temps now average around 80c, sometimes peaking at 90c.
Bottom line is that if you're going to be using this for CPU intensive tasks definitely pair this with an AIO.
